notes: Bundibugyo virus identified by INRB; cases span 13 health zones across Ituri / Nord-Kivu / Sud-Kivu provinces (Ituri remains epicenter; Sud-Kivu first lab-confirmed case 2026-05-25). CDC Travel Notice escalated from Level 2 to Level 3 after the 2026-05-16 CDC Situation Summary publication. Africa CDC declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) on 2026-05-18 (https://africacdc.org/news-item/u-s-travel-restrictions-related-to-the-bundibugyo-ebola-outbreak/). US State Department Travel Advisory at Level 4 (Do Not Travel) for DRC; US entry restrictions in effect from 2026-05-22 on non-US passport holders who travelled to DRC in the previous 21 days, extended to green-card holders the same week; CDC Title 42 Order in effect for arrivals from DRC (https://www.cdc.gov/media/releases/2026/statement-update-on-title-42-order.html). US arrivals from affected countries funneled through IAD (from 2026-05-21), ATL (from 2026-05-22), and IAH Houston (from 2026-05-26) for enhanced screening. On 2026-05-31 the DRC government and WHO issued a joint statement explicitly asking other governments to keep borders open (https://www.who.int/news/item/31-05-2026-joint-statement-by-the-government-of-the-democratic-republic-of-the-congo-and-who-concerning-the-outbreak-of-ebola-disease-caused-by-the-bundibugyo-virus). 2026-06-15: CDC re-reviewed the DRC Level 3 notice (page now dated 15 June 2026); the affected provinces (Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu) remain Level 3 (Reconsider Nonessential Travel), with non-affected DRC provinces now covered under the combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice (https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/ebola-drc-uganda). DRC Level 3 URL and level unchanged. 2026-07-12: the DRC Institut National de Sante Publique formally designated Haut-Uele and Tshopo as epidemic zones (4 cases including 2 deaths in Tshopo, 1 death in Haut-Uele, all judged imported from Nia Nia HZ in Ituri), taking the outbreak from 3 to 5 affected provinces (Reuters via CNBC Africa https://www.cnbcafrica.com/2026/congo-says-ebola-outbreak-spreads-to-provinces-haut-uele-and-tshopo). CDC has NOT re-scoped its Level 3 notice, which still names only Ituri, Nord-Kivu and Sud-Kivu; watch for a re-scope. 2026-07-15: CDC re-scoped the DRC Level 3 notice (page last reviewed 15 July 2026) to name Haut-Uele, Ituri, Nord-Kivu (North Kivu) and Tshopo provinces, adding the two provinces designated epidemic zones on 12 July; Sud-Kivu is no longer listed among the affected provinces. The combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice (https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/ebola-drc-uganda) was updated the same day to reflect the new affected-provinces list. Level unchanged at Level 3; cdc_advisory and who_status unchanged.

case_status: Outbreak declared OVER by Uganda MoH 2026-07-28 (ahead of the WHO 42-day window); final counts 20 confirmed / 18 recovered / 2 deaths
cdc_advisory: HAN-00530 (Health Alert); enhanced travel screening from 2026-05-18
who_status: Included in joint PHEIC (2026-05-17); Uganda MoH declared the outbreak over 2026-07-28; WHO acknowledged the declaration in DON614 (1 August 2026) and is monitoring for 42 days from the 16 July discharge of the most recent imported case
notes: Initial cases imported from DRC (May 15-16); healthcare-worker cases in Kampala were contacts under follow-up per Uganda MoH (not undetected community transmission). 2026-05-27: Uganda ordered border with DRC closed "with immediate effect" for four weeks (Ebola response teams, humanitarian, cargo, security exempted, subject to mandatory 21-day isolation). Measure goes against WHO guidance, which warns closures push movement to unmonitored informal crossings. 2026-05-27: CDC raised Uganda Travel Health Notice from Level 1 (Practice Usual Precautions) to Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions), per the US Embassy Kampala 28 May health alert (https://ug.usembassy.gov/health-alert-u-s-embassy-kampala-uganda-may-28-2026/). US State Department Travel Advisory for Uganda at Level 4 (Do Not Travel). US entry restrictions on non-US passport holders who travelled to Uganda in the previous 21 days (from 2026-05-22, extended to green-card holders same week); CDC Title 42 Order in effect for arrivals from Uganda. Africa CDC declared a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) on 2026-05-18 covering both DRC and Uganda. 2026-06-15: CDC re-reviewed the Bundibugyo Travel Health Notices (both per-country pages now dated 15 June 2026) and consolidated the standalone Uganda Level 2 notice into a combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice at https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/ebola-drc-uganda (the old /level2/ebola-uganda URL now redirects there); Uganda level unchanged at Level 2 (Practice Enhanced Precautions). cdc_travel_notice_url updated accordingly. 2026-07-15: CDC re-reviewed the combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice (page last reviewed 15 July 2026); Uganda level unchanged at Level 2. 2026-07-16: WHO reported Uganda's last confirmed Ebola patient was discharged from care after testing negative twice, starting the 42-day countdown before the outbreak can be declared over (WHO DG media briefing 16 July; WHO AFRO https://www.afro.who.int/countries/uganda/news/uganda-begins-countdown-end-ebola-outbreak). Uganda holds at 20 confirmed cases / 2 deaths (15 imported from DRC, 5 local). WHO Sitrep 09 additionally tracks 1 probable Uganda case / 1 probable death. Country remains at risk of re-importation while DRC transmission continues. 2026-07-28: Uganda's Ministry of Health officially declared the 2026 Ebola outbreak OVER, Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi announcing "Today, Uganda is Ebola-free" ([Xinhua 28 July](https://english.news.cn/20260728/b8f2e1310c254e6fa74e6072b4294de6/c.html); [New Vision](https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/news/uganda-is-officially-ebola-free-minister-bary-NV_237841_072026)). The declaration came BEFORE the completion of WHO's standard 42-day countdown (last patient discharged 16 July after two negative tests); the MoH justified it on full epidemiological characterisation -- outbreak source identified, transmission chains completely reconstructed, all confirmed cases epidemiologically linked, all contacts successfully followed up, and enhanced nationwide surveillance detecting no further community transmission -- arguing the 42-day criterion need not be the sole basis when an imported outbreak is fully characterised. Final Uganda counts: 20 confirmed cases (15 imported from DRC, 5 local), 18 recoveries, 2 deaths. Baryomunsi warned Ebola remains a threat while transmission continues in neighbouring DRC; Uganda will maintain surveillance and border-district preparedness. CDC Travel Notice unchanged this run: the combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice (https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/notices/level2/ebola-drc-uganda) still reads Level 2 for Uganda, page last reviewed 15 July 2026 (CDC has not yet reflected the declaration). WHO formal end-of-outbreak concurrence not yet issued as of this run. 2026-08-01: WHO formally acknowledged Uganda's end-of-outbreak declaration in [Disease Outbreak News DON614](https://www.who.int/emergencies/disease-outbreak-news/item/2026-DON614), and in doing so corrected this tracker's earlier reading that Uganda declared ahead of the 42-day window. WHO's account is that the declaration followed 42 days with no new confirmed locally transmitted case, counting from the discharge of the last locally transmitted case on 16 June 2026; the 16 July discharge was of the most recent IMPORTED case, and WHO is running a separate 42-day monitoring period from that date. So the 42-day criterion on local transmission was met, and the residual clock covers importation, not local chains. WHO reiterates that Uganda remains at risk of re-importation while transmission continues in DR Congo and calls for heightened surveillance and preparedness. This is WHO acknowledgement, not yet a WHO end-of-outbreak concurrence statement of its own. 2026-08-02: CDC Travel Health Notices re-verified via Chrome on the per-country pages; the combined DRC+Uganda Level 2 notice still covers Uganda and non-affected DRC provinces, page last reviewed 15 July 2026. CDC has still not reflected the 28 July declaration. Level unchanged.
